state.case_summary:
A 22-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus was readmitted with fever and a generalized eruption. Six days prior to this admission, she had been hospitalized for a photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (ACLE).

Temperature of 101.5°F. Examination revealed:- Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead- Several large bullae on the right arm- Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles- Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm

Laboratory Tests:- Hemogram: Normocytic anemia (mean corpuscular volume: 99 fL; hemoglobin: 11.7 g/dL; hematocrit: 33.4%)- Platelet count: 81 K/μL (thrombocytopenia)- Complement levels: C3 of 42 mg/dL; C4 of 3 mg/dL (hypocomplementemia)- Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:1280 (speckled pattern)- Antidouble-stranded DNA titer: 1:80- Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies- Negative bacterial blood, urine, stool and cerebrospinal fluid cultures- Negative hepatitis panelBiopsy Findings:- Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes- Acute stratum corneum present overlying full thickness epithelial necrosisImages:Image A Title: Malar erythemaDescription: Dusky malar erythema with focal heme crustingImage B Title: Bullae and target lesionsDescription: Flaccid bullae and target lesionsImage C Title: Target lesions of the backDescription: Diffuse typical and atypical target lesions of the backImage D Title: Punch biopsy histopathologyDescription: High-power view (100×) of punch biopsy from left abdomen showing dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
